page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highcpu-8 is a compute-optimized virtual machine belonging to the n4 server family. It is configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical Intel cores using the x86_64 architecture with hyperthreading enabled. The instance features 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs. The processor features a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache, alongside advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and int8 operations.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance delivers mid-range performance across most compute and memory metrics. The single-core stress-ng CPU score is 1672.09, and the multi-core score is 7217.53. Memory bandwidth tests show read speeds of 568.81 GB/sec for small cached blocks, which drops to 68.85 GB/sec for larger uncached blocks, alongside a write speed of 40.33 GB/sec. Passmark memory testing rates the memory subsystem as weak, scoring 1718.22. However, the CPU handles specialized workloads effectively, achieving a Geekbench compiling score of 8701.0 and a ray tracing score of 9855.0.

This server is designed for compute-bound tasks that do not require massive memory footprints. It achieves 8.82 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and a static web serving throughput of 11.89 GB/sec. For machine learning, the hardware-assisted AMX instructions support small-scale LLM inference, processing 692.71 tokens per second for prompt processing on a 135M model, though performance drops to a weak 7.92 tokens per second for text generation on a 7B model. The lack of local storage and lower memory allocation per core represent clear tradeoffs, making it less suitable for large-scale databases but highly cost-efficient for web serving, software compilation, and lightweight vector calculations.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4-highcpu-8 is an x86_64 compute-optimized virtual machine featuring 8 dedicated Intel vCPUs across 4 physical cores and 16.0 GB of RAM. Lacking local storage and GPU accelerators, this instance focuses on raw CPU execution, supported by a large 260 MB L3 cache and advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and Intel AMX. Benchmark data shows average multi-core performance with a Geekbench score of 7215.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 7217.53. While its memory subsystem is relatively weak under heavy synthetic loads, it maintains high throughput for specific applications, delivering 8.82 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 11.89 GB/sec in static web serving. The 2.0 GB per vCPU memory ratio makes it a cost-efficient choice for compute-heavy, memory-light workloads such as software compilation, web serving, and moderate vector mathematics.
